Maya: heads-up: noticed latency tailpop after yesterday's coalesce-jitter tweak on canary.  p95 up ~18% for short prompts (<=16 tokens) :thinking_face:
Arjun: ugh. which model/commit?
Maya: rwd-small-v2 on canary, commit 6f3a2b; runtime switched kernel selector to prefer fused-attn int8 path when seq_len<=32.
Lee: any flamegraphs/profiles?
Maya: uploading flamegraph now — link: https://perf.internal/redwood/fg/350987 — main hotspot is time spent in kernel-friendly layout transform + extra memcpy in coalesce path.
Sofia: KV hit ratio changed too? we saw per-request kv lookup time increase on same hosts. maybe cache sharding or priming got worse with microbatching shift.
Maya: good catch. KV hit ratio dropped from 0.91 -> 0.82 for those tenants during the window. correlated with bigger micro-batches (avg batch size 3.6 -> 6.1).
Arjun: bigger batch size = more KV priming churn since we wait longer and more distinct contexts accumulate. any change to micro-batch interval or coalesce delay?
Maya: yes — we increased micro-batch interval from 5ms -> 12ms and added gaussian jitter 0-6ms to reduce synchronized wakes. that reduced some stabby tails elsewhere but seems to worsen KV locality for short requests.
Lee: kernel selector preferring fused-int8 may reduce compute cost per-token but adds layout conversion cost that doesn't amortize on tiny batches. combined with higher coalesce delay it amplifies end-to-end latency.
Sofia: repro plan: run synthetic workload of short prompts (8 tokens) with arrival poisson lam=50 req/s, compare these configs: (A) interval=5ms jitter=2ms kernel=auto (B) interval=12ms jitter=6ms kernel=auto (C) interval=12ms jitter=6ms kernel=force-fp16
Maya: I ran a quick bench, results below (p50/p95 in ms):
```
Config A: 12 / 38
Config B: 16 / 45
Config C: 18 / 39
```
Maya: so forcing fp16 kernel raises p50 slightly but improves p95 vs B. suggests kernel layout cost is hurting tail.
Arjun: interesting. what's KV hit ratio in those runs?
Maya: A: 0.90, B: 0.83, C: 0.84
Lee: that aligns. hypothesis: longer coalesce delays allow more distinct requests to join batch, increasing KV working set and eviction pressure; fused-int8 layout transforms exacerbate per-request overhead when batch isn't large enough.
Sofia: possible mitigations: reduce max coalesce_delay for short-request lanes via queue policy; add adaptive jitter that shrinks when measured KV hit_ratio < 0.88; or bias kernel selector to prefer fp16 for batch_size<=4.
Arjun: prefer lightweight rule first: tweak queue policy to cap interval to 6ms for the 'short-prompt' token_budget route. low-risk rollback.
Maya: agree. I can push a canary to route short-token requests with interval=6ms, jitter=2ms, kernel_hint=prefer-fp16.
deploy-bot: deploy started: service=runtime-canary cfg=short-window-6ms by=Maya
perf-bot: perf tests running: synthetic short-prompt sweep (A/B/C)
Maya: also adding a quick telemetry gauge to surface KV hit ratio per-route so we catch this earlier.
Lee: also log per-request kernel path chosen so we can correlate layout conversions to latency. keep logs sampled 1% to avoid noise.
Arjun: timeline? small canary out in 30m, monitor for ~2 hours and check p95 + KV hit_ratio + kernel_path distribution.
Sofia: if canary looks good, roll to tiered canary for a day before global. If not, rollback and revert jitter change.
Maya: noted. will post status updates here. thanks all :thumbsup:
Maya: (follow-up after 2h) quick update: canary p95 down from 45->36, KV hit_ratio back to 0.89, kernel_path fp16% increased from 22%->71% on short-route. looks promising.
Arjun: +1 to expand to more hosts. keep an eye on cost impact (fp16 more expensive?).
Lee: file a small perf ticket to track longer-term: kernel_selector heuristics should consider downstream KV locality signals when choosing layout-heavy kernels.
Maya: filed PERF-1298 with notes + attachments.
